# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

def parse_int_value(opt_long: str, metavar: str, val: str) -> int:
    try:
        # Rust's integer parser accepts only unsigned decimal here. A leading
        # '-' normally becomes an unexpected argument before this point when the
        # value is separated; for --opt=-1 this message is close enough.
        if val == "" or not val.isdecimal():
            raise ValueError
        return int(val, 10)
    except Exception:
        clap_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--{opt_long} {metavar}': invalid digit found in string")


def need_value(args: list[str], i: int, opt_long: str, metavar: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    if i + 1 >= len(args) or args[i + 1].startswith('-'):
        clap_error(f"a value is required for '--{opt_long} {metavar}' but none was supplied")
    return args[i + 1], i + 1


def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> Options:
    opts = Options()
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg in ("-h", "--help"):
            sys.stdout.write(help_text())
            raise SystemExit(0)
        if arg.startswith("--"):
            body = arg[2:]
            value_inline = None
            if "=" in body:
                body, value_inline = body.split("=", 1)
            if body in FLAGS:
                if value_inline is not None:
                    clap_error(f"unexpected value '{value_inline}' for '--{body}' found; no more were expected", f"--{body}")
                setattr(opts, FLAGS[body], True)
            elif body in VALUE_LONG:
                attr, metavar, typ = VALUE_LONG[body]
                if value_inline is None:
                    val, i = need_value(argv, i, body, metavar)
                else:
                    val = value_inline
                if typ is int:
                    val2 = parse_int_value(body, metavar, val)
                else:
                    val2 = val
                setattr(opts, attr, val2)
            else:
                clap_error(f"unexpected argument '--{body}' found", "[OPTIONS]")
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            # Short options with attached values, matching clap's behaviour for
            # the value-taking short flags used by this program.
            if arg == "-h":
                sys.stdout.write(help_text())
                raise SystemExit(0)
            flag = arg[1:2]
            rest = arg[2:]
            if flag not in VALUE_SHORT:
                clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{arg}' found", "[OPTIONS]")
            long = VALUE_SHORT[flag]
            attr, metavar, typ = VALUE_LONG[long]
            if rest:
                val = rest[1:] if rest.startswith("=") else rest
            else:
                val, i = need_value(argv, i, long, metavar)
            if typ is int:
                val2 = parse_int_value(long, metavar, val)
            else:
                val2 = val
            setattr(opts, attr, val2)
        else:
            clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{arg}' found", "[OPTIONS]")
        i += 1
    return opts

        ("combi", opts.combi, 1, 200, "Invalid argument for combi. Use a number between 1 and 200."),
        ("rep", opts.rep, 1, 200, "Invalid argument for rep. Use a number between 1 and 200."),
        ("wpm", opts.wpm, 1, 200, "Invalid argument for wpm. Use a number between 1 and 200."),
        ("acc", opts.acc, 0, 100, "Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100."),
    ]
    for _name, val, lo, hi, msg in checks:
        if not (lo <= val <= hi):

    if bool(opts.emu_in) != bool(opts.emu_out):

def layout_transform(ch: str, src_name: str, dst_name: str) -> str:
    if not src_name or not dst_name:
        return ch
    src = get_layout(src_name)
    dst = get_layout(dst_name)
    for r, row in enumerate(src):
        for c, key in enumerate(row):
            if key == ch and r < len(dst) and c < len(dst[r]):
                return dst[r][c]
    return ch


def make_lesson(items: list[str], opts: Options) -> str:
    top_items = items[:max(1, min(opts.top, len(items)))] or [""]
    # Draw combi ngrams (duplicates possible when combi > available, as with top=1)
    chosen = [random.choice(top_items) for _ in range(opts.combi)]
    parts: list[str] = []
    for item in chosen:
        for _ in range(opts.rep):
            parts.append(item)
    return " ".join(parts)


def line_with_content(content: str, width: int = 79) -> str:
    inner = width - 2
    if len(content) > inner:
        content = content[:inner]
    return "│" + content + " " * (inner - len(content)) + "│"


def centered(content: str, width: int = 79) -> str:
    inner = width - 2
    if len(content) > inner:
        content = content[:inner]
    left = (inner - len(content)) // 2
    return "│" + " " * left + content + " " * (inner - left - len(content)) + "│"

def render(opts: Options, lesson: str, typed: str, lesson_no: int, ok: int, bad: int,
           last_wpm: int, last_acc: int, avg_wpm: int, avg_acc: int) -> str:
    width = 79
    lines: list[str] = []
    top = "╭" + "─" * 65 + " Quit " + BOLD + BLUE + "<esc> " + NORMAL_INTENSITY + FG_RESET + "╮"
    lines.append(top)
    title = "" + " " * 19 + BOLD + "               ngrrram!" + NORMAL_INTENSITY + ITALIC + GRAY + "   by winterveil" + NOT_ITALIC + FG_RESET
    lines.append(line_with_content(title))
    lines.append("│" + "─" * 77 + "│")
    counter = f"    Lesson     #{lesson_no}"
    right = f"{GREEN}✔: {ok}, {RED}✘: {bad}    {FG_RESET}"
    inner = counter + " " * max(1, 77 - len(counter) - len(f"✔: {ok}, ✘: {bad}    ")) + right
    lines.append("│" + inner + "│")
    lines.append("│" + "─" * 77 + "│")
    lines.append(line_with_content(""))
    target_line = visible_prefix_match(lesson, typed)
    lines.append(centered(BOLD + target_line + NORMAL_INTENSITY))
    typed_line = typed[-67:]
    lines.append(centered(ITALIC + GRAY + typed_line + RESET))
    if not opts.nokb:
        kbl = keyboard_lines(opts.emu_out or "qwerty", opts.show_ortho, opts.cat)
        # Replace/extend around the observed area.
        lines.append(kbl[0])

    acc_line = f"  need >= {opts.acc:3d}% Acc, avg. {avg_acc}%Acc, last{last_acc}%Acc"

    lines.append("╰" + "─" * 77 + "╯")
    return "\x1b[1;1H" + "\n".join(lines) + RESET


class PracticeApp:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options, items: list[str]):
        self.opts = opts
        self.items = items
        self.lesson_no = 1
        self.ok = 0
        self.bad = 0
        self.last_wpm = 0
        self.last_acc = 0
        self.avg_wpm = 0
        self.avg_acc = 0
        self.wpm_values: list[int] = []
        self.acc_values: list[int] = []
        self.lesson = make_lesson(items, opts)
        self.typed = ""
        self.started_at: float | None = None
        self.running = True

    def finish_lesson(self) -> None:
        elapsed = max(0.001, time.time() - (self.started_at or time.time()))
        total = len(self.typed)
        target = self.lesson
        correct = sum(1 for a, b in zip(self.typed, target) if a == b)
        self.last_acc = int(round((correct / total) * 100)) if total else 0
        chars = len(target.replace(" ", ""))
        self.last_wpm = int(round((chars / 5.0) / (elapsed / 60.0))) if elapsed > 0 else 0
        success = self.last_wpm >= self.opts.wpm and self.last_acc >= self.opts.acc and self.typed == target
        if success:
            self.ok += 1
        else:
            self.bad += 1
        self.wpm_values.append(self.last_wpm)
        self.acc_values.append(self.last_acc)
        self.avg_wpm = int(round(sum(self.wpm_values) / len(self.wpm_values)))
        self.avg_acc = int(round(sum(self.acc_values) / len(self.acc_values)))
        self.lesson_no += 1
        self.lesson = make_lesson(self.items, self.opts)
        self.typed = ""
        self.started_at = None

    def feed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        for b in data:
            if b in (3,):  # Ctrl-C
                raise KeyboardInterrupt
            if b == 27:  # Escape
                self.running = False
                return
            if b in (8, 127):
                self.typed = self.typed[:-1]
                continue
            if b in (10, 13):
                # The observed app does not need Enter, but accepting it makes
                # line-oriented test input harmless.
                continue
            try:
                ch = bytes([b]).decode("utf-8")
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                continue
            if not ch.isprintable():
                continue
            if self.started_at is None:
                self.started_at = time.time()
            ch = layout_transform(ch, self.opts.emu_in, self.opts.emu_out)
            self.typed += ch
            if len(self.typed) >= len(self.lesson):
                self.finish_lesson()

    def screen(self) -> str:
        return render(self.opts, self.lesson, self.typed, self.lesson_no,
                      self.ok, self.bad, self.last_wpm, self.last_acc,
                      self.avg_wpm, self.avg_acc)


def run_tui(opts: Options, items: list[str]) -> int:
    # The original enters the alternate screen and then fails when there is no
    # terminal device; reproduce the visible behaviour for non-interactive runs.
    if not sys.stdin.isatty() or not sys.stdout.isatty():
        sys.stdout.write(ALT_ON)
        sys.stdout.flush()
        sys.stderr.write('Error: Os { code: 6, kind: Uncategorized, message: "No such device or address" }\n')
        return 1

    app = PracticeApp(opts, items)
    old_attrs = termios.tcgetattr(sys.stdin.fileno())
    def cleanup(*_args):
        try:
            termios.tcsetattr(sys.stdin.fileno(), termios.TCSADRAIN, old_attrs)
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            sys.stdout.write(RESET + ALT_OFF)
            sys.stdout.flush()
        except Exception:
            pass
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda signum, frame: (cleanup(), sys.exit(0)))
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, lambda signum, frame: (_ for _ in ()).throw(KeyboardInterrupt()))
    try:
        tty.setcbreak(sys.stdin.fileno())
        sys.stdout.write(ALT_ON + CLEAR + app.screen())
        sys.stdout.flush()
        last_draw = 0.0
        while app.running:
            r, _, _ = select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], 0.08)
            if r:
                data = os.read(sys.stdin.fileno(), 32)
                app.feed(data)
                sys.stdout.write(app.screen())
                sys.stdout.flush()
                last_draw = time.time()
            elif time.time() - last_draw > 0.5:
                # The original redraws regularly; doing so also helps tests that
                # capture after a small delay.
                sys.stdout.write(app.screen())
                sys.stdout.flush()
                last_draw = time.time()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        cleanup()
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    try:
        opts = parse_args(sys.argv[1:])
        validate_options(opts)
        items = load_items(opts.n)
        return run_tui(opts, items)
    except BrokenPipeError:
        return 0

    raise SystemExit(main())

def clap_error(message: str, usage: str | None = None) -> None:
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: {message}\n\n")
    if usage:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Usage: {progname()} {usage}\n\n")
    sys.stderr.write("For more information, try '--help'.\n")
    raise SystemExit(2)

    "wpm": ("wpm", "<number>", int),

def parse_int_value(opt_long: str, metavar: str, val: str) -> int:
    try:
        # Rust's integer parser accepts only unsigned decimal here. A leading
        # '-' normally becomes an unexpected argument before this point when the
        # value is separated; for --opt=-1 this message is close enough.
        if val == "" or not val.isdecimal():
            raise ValueError
        return int(val, 10)
    except Exception:
        clap_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--{opt_long} {metavar}': invalid digit found in string")


def need_value(args: list[str], i: int, opt_long: str, metavar: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    if i + 1 >= len(args) or args[i + 1].startswith('-'):
        clap_error(f"a value is required for '--{opt_long} {metavar}' but none was supplied")
    return args[i + 1], i + 1


def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> Options:
    opts = Options()
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg in ("-h", "--help"):
            sys.stdout.write(help_text())
            raise SystemExit(0)
        if arg.startswith("--"):
            body = arg[2:]
            value_inline = None
            if "=" in body:
                body, value_inline = body.split("=", 1)
            if body in FLAGS:
                if value_inline is not None:
                    clap_error(f"unexpected value '{value_inline}' for '--{body}' found; no more were expected", f"--{body}")
                setattr(opts, FLAGS[body], True)
            elif body in VALUE_LONG:
                attr, metavar, typ = VALUE_LONG[body]
                if value_inline is None:
                    val, i = need_value(argv, i, body, metavar)
                else:
                    val = value_inline
                if typ is int:
                    val2 = parse_int_value(body, metavar, val)
                else:
                    val2 = val
                setattr(opts, attr, val2)
            else:
                clap_error(f"unexpected argument '--{body}' found", "[OPTIONS]")
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            # Short options with attached values, matching clap's behaviour for
            # the value-taking short flags used by this program.
            if arg == "-h":
                sys.stdout.write(help_text())
                raise SystemExit(0)
            flag = arg[1:2]
            rest = arg[2:]
            if flag not in VALUE_SHORT:
                clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{arg}' found", "[OPTIONS]")
            long = VALUE_SHORT[flag]
            attr, metavar, typ = VALUE_LONG[long]
            if rest:
                val = rest[1:] if rest.startswith("=") else rest
            else:
                val, i = need_value(argv, i, long, metavar)
            if typ is int:
                val2 = parse_int_value(long, metavar, val)
            else:
                val2 = val
            setattr(opts, attr, val2)
        else:
            clap_error(f"unexpected argument '{arg}' found", "[OPTIONS]")
        i += 1
    return opts


def validate_options(opts: Options) -> None:
    checks = [
        ("top", opts.top, 1, 200, "Invalid argument for top. Use a number between 1 and 200."),
        ("combi", opts.combi, 1, 200, "Invalid argument for combi. Use a number between 1 and 200."),
        ("rep", opts.rep, 1, 200, "Invalid argument for rep. Use a number between 1 and 200."),
        ("wpm", opts.wpm, 1, 200, "Invalid argument for wpm. Use a number between 1 and 200."),
        ("acc", opts.acc, 0, 100, "Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100."),
    ]
    for _name, val, lo, hi, msg in checks:
        if not (lo <= val <= hi):
            print(msg)
            raise SystemExit(1)
    if bool(opts.emu_in) != bool(opts.emu_out):
        print("You need to specify both emu_in and emu_out.")
        raise SystemExit(1)


def load_items(nopt: str) -> list[str]:
    if nopt == "2":
        return BIGRAMS[:]
    if nopt == "3":
        return TRIGRAMS[:]
    if nopt == "4":
        return TETRAGRAMS[:]
    if nopt == "w":
        return WORDS[:]
    if not os.path.exists(nopt):
        print(f"File not found: {nopt}")
        raise SystemExit(1)
    with open(nopt, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        data = f.read()
    # The documentation says comma separated; the original preserves spaces.
    return data.split(',') if data != "" else [""]


def get_layout(name: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    return LAYOUTS.get(name.lower(), LAYOUTS["qwerty"])


def layout_transform(ch: str, src_name: str, dst_name: str) -> str:
    if not src_name or not dst_name:
        return ch
    src = get_layout(src_name)
    dst = get_layout(dst_name)
    for r, row in enumerate(src):
        for c, key in enumerate(row):
            if key == ch and r < len(dst) and c < len(dst[r]):
                return dst[r][c]
    return ch


def make_lesson(items: list[str], opts: Options) -> str:
    top_items = items[:max(1, min(opts.top, len(items)))] or [""]
    # Draw combi ngrams (duplicates possible when combi > available, as with top=1)
    chosen = [random.choice(top_items) for _ in range(opts.combi)]
    parts: list[str] = []
    for item in chosen:
        for _ in range(opts.rep):
            parts.append(item)
    return " ".join(parts)


def line_with_content(content: str, width: int = 79) -> str:
    inner = width - 2
    if len(content) > inner:
        content = content[:inner]
    return "│" + content + " " * (inner - len(content)) + "│"


def centered(content: str, width: int = 79) -> str:
    inner = width - 2
    if len(content) > inner:
        content = content[:inner]
    left = (inner - len(content)) // 2
    return "│" + " " * left + content + " " * (inner - left - len(content)) + "│"

def visible_prefix_match(target: str, typed: str) -> str:
    # Plain visible rendering of the current lesson line. The original uses
    # styles for correct/incorrect characters; this keeps the text stable.
    maxw = 67
    s = target
    return s[:maxw]


def render(opts: Options, lesson: str, typed: str, lesson_no: int, ok: int, bad: int,
           last_wpm: int, last_acc: int, avg_wpm: int, avg_acc: int) -> str:
    width = 79
    lines: list[str] = []
    top = "╭" + "─" * 65 + " Quit " + BOLD + BLUE + "<esc> " + NORMAL_INTENSITY + FG_RESET + "╮"
    lines.append(top)
    title = "" + " " * 19 + BOLD + "               ngrrram!" + NORMAL_INTENSITY + ITALIC + GRAY + "   by winterveil" + NOT_ITALIC + FG_RESET
    lines.append(line_with_content(title))
    lines.append("│" + "─" * 77 + "│")
    counter = f"    Lesson     #{lesson_no}"
    right = f"{GREEN}✔: {ok}, {RED}✘: {bad}    {FG_RESET}"
    inner = counter + " " * max(1, 77 - len(counter) - len(f"✔: {ok}, ✘: {bad}    ")) + right
    lines.append("│" + inner + "│")
    lines.append("│" + "─" * 77 + "│")
    lines.append(line_with_content(""))
    target_line = visible_prefix_match(lesson, typed)
    lines.append(centered(BOLD + target_line + NORMAL_INTENSITY))
    typed_line = typed[-67:]
    lines.append(centered(ITALIC + GRAY + typed_line + RESET))
    if not opts.nokb:
        kbl = keyboard_lines(opts.emu_out or "qwerty", opts.show_ortho, opts.cat)
        # Replace/extend around the observed area.
        lines.append(kbl[0])
        lines.extend(kbl[1:])
    else:
        lines.append(line_with_content(""))
    lines.append("│" + "─" * 77 + "│")
    wpm_line = f"  need >= {opts.wpm:3d}WPM,   avg. {avg_wpm}WPM,   last{last_wpm}WPM"
    acc_line = f"  need >= {opts.acc:3d}% Acc, avg. {avg_acc}%Acc, last{last_acc}%Acc"
    lines.append(line_with_content(GRAY + wpm_line + FG_RESET))
    lines.append(line_with_content(GRAY + acc_line + FG_RESET))
    lines.append("╰" + "─" * 77 + "╯")
    return "\x1b[1;1H" + "\n".join(lines) + RESET


class PracticeApp:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options, items: list[str]):
        self.opts = opts
        self.items = items
        self.lesson_no = 1
        self.ok = 0
        self.bad = 0
        self.last_wpm = 0
        self.last_acc = 0
        self.avg_wpm = 0
        self.avg_acc = 0
        self.wpm_values: list[int] = []
        self.acc_values: list[int] = []
        self.lesson = make_lesson(items, opts)
        self.typed = ""
        self.started_at: float | None = None
        self.running = True

    def finish_lesson(self) -> None:
        elapsed = max(0.001, time.time() - (self.started_at or time.time()))
        total = len(self.typed)
        target = self.lesson
        correct = sum(1 for a, b in zip(self.typed, target) if a == b)
        self.last_acc = int(round((correct / total) * 100)) if total else 0
        chars = len(target.replace(" ", ""))
        self.last_wpm = int(round((chars / 5.0) / (elapsed / 60.0))) if elapsed > 0 else 0
        success = self.last_wpm >= self.opts.wpm and self.last_acc >= self.opts.acc and self.typed == target
        if success:
            self.ok += 1
        else:
            self.bad += 1
        self.wpm_values.append(self.last_wpm)
        self.acc_values.append(self.last_acc)
        self.avg_wpm = int(round(sum(self.wpm_values) / len(self.wpm_values)))
        self.avg_acc = int(round(sum(self.acc_values) / len(self.acc_values)))
        self.lesson_no += 1
        self.lesson = make_lesson(self.items, self.opts)
        self.typed = ""
        self.started_at = None

    def feed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        for b in data:
            if b in (3,):  # Ctrl-C
                raise KeyboardInterrupt
            if b == 27:  # Escape
                self.running = False
                return
            if b in (8, 127):
                self.typed = self.typed[:-1]
                continue
            if b in (10, 13):
                # The observed app does not need Enter, but accepting it makes
                # line-oriented test input harmless.
                continue
            try:
                ch = bytes([b]).decode("utf-8")
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                continue
            if not ch.isprintable():
                continue
            if self.started_at is None:
                self.started_at = time.time()
            ch = layout_transform(ch, self.opts.emu_in, self.opts.emu_out)
            self.typed += ch
            if len(self.typed) >= len(self.lesson):
                self.finish_lesson()

    def screen(self) -> str:
        return render(self.opts, self.lesson, self.typed, self.lesson_no,
                      self.ok, self.bad, self.last_wpm, self.last_acc,
                      self.avg_wpm, self.avg_acc)


def run_tui(opts: Options, items: list[str]) -> int:
    # The original enters the alternate screen and then fails when there is no
    # terminal device; reproduce the visible behaviour for non-interactive runs.
    if not sys.stdin.isatty() or not sys.stdout.isatty():
        sys.stdout.write(ALT_ON)
        sys.stdout.flush()
        sys.stderr.write('Error: Os { code: 6, kind: Uncategorized, message: "No such device or address" }\n')
        return 1

    app = PracticeApp(opts, items)
    old_attrs = termios.tcgetattr(sys.stdin.fileno())
    def cleanup(*_args):
        try:
            termios.tcsetattr(sys.stdin.fileno(), termios.TCSADRAIN, old_attrs)
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            sys.stdout.write(RESET + ALT_OFF)
            sys.stdout.flush()
        except Exception:
            pass
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda signum, frame: (cleanup(), sys.exit(0)))
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, lambda signum, frame: (_ for _ in ()).throw(KeyboardInterrupt()))
    try:
        tty.setcbreak(sys.stdin.fileno())
        sys.stdout.write(ALT_ON + CLEAR + app.screen())
        sys.stdout.flush()
        last_draw = 0.0
        while app.running:
            r, _, _ = select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], 0.08)
            if r:
                data = os.read(sys.stdin.fileno(), 32)
                app.feed(data)
                sys.stdout.write(app.screen())
                sys.stdout.flush()
                last_draw = time.time()
            elif time.time() - last_draw > 0.5:
                # The original redraws regularly; doing so also helps tests that
                # capture after a small delay.
                sys.stdout.write(app.screen())
                sys.stdout.flush()
                last_draw = time.time()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        cleanup()
    return 0
